<!--
Read CONTRIBUTING.md before you open a pull request. Solve one problem.
A draft meets the same rules. The title becomes the release note, so
write it as the sentence you want a reader to find there.
-->

## Problem

<!-- Say what is wrong in a sentence or two. Where it helps, say what
you expected and how to reproduce it. -->

## Change

<!-- Say how this change solves the problem. If it touches several
parts, say why the one fix needs each of them. Send an independent fix
in its own pull request. -->

## Scope and approval

<!-- Link the issue this closes, or the discussion where the idea was
accepted. A bug fix, a typo or a broken link needs neither: say which
one this is. -->

## Verification

<!-- Say which tests or checks you ran and what you saw. State anything
you could not check. "Tests pass" alone is not enough.

Where the change shows on screen, add before and after screenshots, and
a short recording where motion or timing matters. Upload them to GitHub
and embed or link them here. Do not commit them. -->

<!-- If you used an agent, end with the model and the harness that did
the work. -->
